# Run a performance improvement process

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When documented performance concerns need a supported improvement plan beyond routine feedback. A fair, documented review outcome with support delivered and any further action separately authorized.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Assemble factual performance evidence

agent-runnable


Gather the role expectations, prior feedback, work examples and relevant dates. Separate capability, conduct, workload and unclear objectives, and restrict the record to those responsible for the process.

- Sources: [Acas problems with employee performance](https://www.acas.org.uk/performance-management/problems-with-an-employees-performance) · [Acas disciplinary and grievance procedures](https://www.acas.org.uk/acas-code-of-practice-on-disciplinary-and-grievance-procedures/html)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Assess causes and the appropriate process

human · human approval required


The manager and HR hear the employee's perspective and review support, health, disability or workplace factors with qualified advice where needed. Choose the applicable informal or formal route without prejudging dismissal.

- Sources: [Acas problems with employee performance](https://www.acas.org.uk/performance-management/problems-with-an-employees-performance) · [Acas disciplinary and grievance procedures](https://www.acas.org.uk/acas-code-of-practice-on-disciplinary-and-grievance-procedures/html)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Agree a specific improvement and support plan

human · human approval required


Set observable expectations, resources, coaching, review points and responsibilities. Check the plan is realistic for the role and circumstances and explain how progress and concerns will be discussed.

- Sources: [Acas problems with employee performance](https://www.acas.org.uk/performance-management/problems-with-an-employees-performance) · [Acas disciplinary and grievance procedures](https://www.acas.org.uk/acas-code-of-practice-on-disciplinary-and-grievance-procedures/html)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Deliver support and review evidence

human · human approval required


Hold the agreed check-ins, provide the promised resources and record both progress and unresolved barriers. Reassess the plan when facts change rather than manufacturing a record for a predetermined outcome.

- Sources: [Acas problems with employee performance](https://www.acas.org.uk/performance-management/problems-with-an-employees-performance) · [Acas disciplinary and grievance procedures](https://www.acas.org.uk/acas-code-of-practice-on-disciplinary-and-grievance-procedures/html)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Decide and document the outcome

human · human approval required


The authorized manager and HR review the evidence and applicable process before deciding whether to close, extend or escalate. Any contractual change, disciplinary action or termination requires its own reviewed authority and communication.

- Verify: A fair, documented review outcome with support delivered and any further action separately authorized.
- Sources: [Acas problems with employee performance](https://www.acas.org.uk/performance-management/problems-with-an-employees-performance) · [Acas disciplinary and grievance procedures](https://www.acas.org.uk/acas-code-of-practice-on-disciplinary-and-grievance-procedures/html)
